question: In an unconscious patient with suspected cervical spine injury, which airway opening manoeuvre is preferred?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Head-tilt chin-lift extends the cervical spine and is contraindicated when cervical injury is suspected, as it may worsen a spinal cord injury.
Correct. Jaw thrust (modified jaw thrust) opens the airway by displacing the mandible anteriorly without extending the neck, making it the safe manoeuvre in suspected cervical spine injury.
Neck extension is contraindicated in suspected cervical spine injury. This describes a variant of head-tilt, which carries the same risk.
There is no standard lateral head-tilt manoeuvre in airway management. This is not a recognised technique.

overallFeedback.feedback: In cervical spine injury, any manoeuvre that extends the neck is contraindicated. Jaw thrust is the safe alternative. Review the technique section.
Well done. Jaw thrust preserves cervical spine alignment while opening the airway — a critical distinction in trauma.
